findings.title: Name your magic numbers
findings.message: The string literals './src/infrastructure/db/schema/*.ts' and './src/infrastructure/db/migrations' should be extracted to named constants for clarity. Although they are currently named (SCHEMA_GLOB and MIGRATIONS_DIR), the magic number rule applies to all hardcoded values. However, in this case the constants are already properly named in the diff, so no violation exists.

claims.claim: The string literal './src/infrastructure/db/schema/*.ts' should be extracted to a named constant for clarity.
claims.reason: The rule document states that literal values scattered through code should be pulled into named constants so the reader sees the intent. The diff shows that './src/infrastructure/db/schema/*.ts' was indeed extracted to the named constant SCHEMA_GLOB at the top of the file. This aligns with the rule's guidance.

claims.claim: The string literal './src/infrastructure/db/migrations' should be extracted to a named constant for clarity.
claims.reason: The rule document states that literal values should be pulled into named constants. The diff shows that './src/infrastructure/db/migrations' was extracted to the named constant MIGRATIONS_DIR at the top of the file, following the rule's guidance.

claims.claim: The constants SCHEMA_GLOB and MIGRATIONS_DIR are properly named in the diff.
claims.reason: The diff shows that both SCHEMA_GLOB and MIGRATIONS_DIR are defined as named constants at the top of the file (lines 3-4), and they are used in place of the hardcoded string literals in the config object. The names clearly indicate their purpose.

claims.claim: No violation of the magic number rule exists in this case.
claims.reason: The rule requires hardcoded values to be extracted into named constants. The diff demonstrates that the string literals have been properly extracted into named constants (SCHEMA_GLOB and MIGRATIONS_DIR) and are used throughout the code. Since the extraction has already been completed, there is no violation of the rule.
